title: Published subprocessor register generated from the vendor inventory
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-SAS-011 requires a per-tenant register of subprocessors (name, function, data classes, location) generated from the vendor inventory. Neither the inventory nor the register exists.
target_answer: Echelon publishes a subprocessor register per tenant, generated from the vendor inventory and from integration configuration, listing each subprocessor's legal entity, function, data categories, processing and support locations and transfer mechanism. Vendors without access to customer data are excluded and the distinction is documented. Because the register is generated from the configuration that actually routes data, an integration that sends customer data to an unlisted party fails a release check.
current_practice: Not established; there are no customers or production data flows.
intended_practice: Generate the register from the vendor inventory (TPR) and a data-flow declaration checked at release.
customer_statement: Echelon plans to publish a per-customer subprocessor list generated from its vendor inventory and data-flow configuration. No list exists yet because no production service processes customer data.

title: Advance notice of subprocessor changes and customer objection rights
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-SAS-011 requires notice to tenant administrators at least 30 days before adding or replacing a subprocessor for that tenant's data, and within 72 hours with reason for emergency replacement. Objection rights are not specified in located requirements.
target_answer: Echelon notifies subscribed customer contacts at least 30 days before adding or replacing a subprocessor, or changing a subprocessor's location or processing scope, with the register diff. Emergency replacements are notified within 72 hours with the reason. Customers may object on reasonable data protection grounds; Echelon then offers an alternative configuration that avoids the subprocessor for that tenant where technically possible, or a termination right with pro-rated refund. Notices are generated from the register diff so none can be skipped.
intended_practice: Implement per UNB-XIN-SAS-011 with objection handling defined in the customer agreement.
customer_statement: Echelon plans 30 days' advance notice of subprocessor changes, 72-hour notice for emergency replacements, and an objection right. Not yet in place.

challenge.customer_intent: Customers want control over who processes their data and time to assess changes.
challenge.adverse_outcome: A new subprocessor with weak controls or in an unacceptable jurisdiction receives customer data without the customer's knowledge.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Notice periods work, but objection rights are rarely exercised and often end only in a right to terminate, which customers cannot practically use.
challenge.legally_required: GDPR Article 28(2) requires prior specific or general written authorization and information about changes with an opportunity to object, where GDPR applies. US law generally does not require this.
challenge.contractually_required: Very common in data processing agreements.
challenge.historical_convention: GDPR-era DPA convention, now applied globally.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Per-tenant routing can make some subprocessors optional so an objecting customer is excluded rather than forced to terminate.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Notices generated from register diffs; data-flow check blocks unlisted subprocessors.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Register history and notice delivery records.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Per-tenant subprocessor selection where feasible, so objection leads to exclusion rather than termination.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Customers can verify their tenant's register and the release check.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely; it gives customers more control than standard terms.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Core infrastructure providers (cloud host) cannot be made optional per tenant.
challenge.alternative_risks: Configuration variety increases testing burden and isolation complexity.
supporting_arguments: Real control instead of a theoretical right.

title: Flow-down terms and oversight of subprocessors
status_rationale: No data processing agreement template or subprocessor contracts were located. SOC2-013 requires contracts and monitoring of subservice organizations; TPR controls would apply.
target_answer: Each subprocessor is bound by written terms at least as protective as Echelon's commitments to the customer: confidentiality, security measures, purpose limitation including no AI training on customer data, breach notice, assistance with data subject requests, deletion at end of service, audit rights and approval of further sub-subprocessors. Echelon remains responsible to the customer for subprocessor performance. Subprocessors are monitored under the TPR program at the tier their data access implies.
intended_practice: Create a DPA template and flow-down checklist; record each subprocessor's terms in the vendor register.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet established subprocessor flow-down terms. It plans to bind subprocessors to terms at least as protective as its customer commitments and to remain responsible for their performance.
residual_risks: Large providers' standard DPAs may not match every customer-specific commitment.

title: Data location, processing location and cross-border transfers
status_rationale: No hosting region, support location or transfer mechanism has been decided in any record located. CNV-ARC-001 specifies one managed PostgreSQL cluster but not its region.
target_answer: Customer data, backups, logs, AI inference and support access are confined to documented regions, by default the United States, enforced by infrastructure configuration and provider region settings and verified by automated configuration checks. Any processing outside the region, including AI inference and follow-the-sun support, is listed in the register with its transfer mechanism (for EU or UK personal data, Standard Contractual Clauses or the Data Privacy Framework where the recipient is certified).
current_practice: Unknown; no production hosting decision located.
intended_practice: Decide hosting region and AI inference region before production and encode them as checked configuration.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet fixed its hosting and processing locations. It intends US-only processing by default, including AI inference, enforced by configuration.
open_questions: Do the AI providers in use offer US-only inference commitments under Echelon's account terms?

title: AI providers as subprocessors
status_rationale: Unbound requires AI inference metering (CNV-ECO-001) and subprocessor notice (UNB-XIN-SAS-011) but does not specify how AI providers appear in the register, which legal entity is the subprocessor when models are reached through a cloud marketplace, or whether engineering AI tools ever receive customer data. Echelon uses AI coding agents whose providers receive repository content.
target_answer: Every AI provider that receives customer content is a listed subprocessor, naming the contracting entity that processes the data (for example the cloud platform hosting a model rather than the model developer, where that is the case), its region and its retention terms. Switching to a new AI provider, or to a different hosting route for a model, triggers the subprocessor notice process; changing model version within the same provider and route does not, but is recorded in the AI inventory. Engineering AI tools never receive customer data, enforced by keeping customer data out of engineering environments; if that ever changes, those providers become subprocessors and are listed.
current_practice: Unknown. AI coding agent providers receive Echelon source and repository content; no customer data exists in engineering environments because there are no customers.
intended_practice: Add AI provider fields to the subprocessor register and a rule keeping customer data out of engineering environments.
customer_statement: Echelon plans to list every AI provider that receives customer content as a subprocessor and to give advance notice before adding or switching one. Its engineering AI tools are not intended to receive customer data. Not yet in place.
